title: Nonlinearity of the Conjecture 12 fiber involution
summary: Determine whether the fixed-point-free involution pairing the two preimages of the Conjecture 12 quadrinomial is nonlinear for every family parameter.

formal_statement.body: For each source-admissible positive integer $m$, put $n=2m+1$ and let $F_m(x)=x+x^3+x^{2^{m+1}}+x^{2^{m+1}+2}$ on $\mathbb F_{2^n}$. For every $x$, let $I_m(x)\ne x$ be the other element of the two-point fiber of $F_m$, so that $F_m(I_m(x))=F_m(x)$. Prove that the source-derived involution $I_m$ has algebraic degree greater than one for every admissible $m$, or exhibit an admissible member for which $I_m$ is affine.

scope.domain: Fixed-point-free finite-field involutions derived from two-to-one mappings for cryptographic S-box design
assumptions: $n=2m+1$ with $m$ in the source-admissible positive-integer range
$I_m$ exchanges the two elements in each nonempty fiber of $F_m$
Nonlinear means non-affine, equivalently algebraic degree greater than one
scope.unresolved_remainder: A later theorem proves that $F_m$ is two-to-one, but two-to-one fiber structure does not imply that the induced fixed-point-free involution is nonlinear. No inspected later result determines the algebraic degree of $I_m$ over the full family.

progress.summary: Conjecture 12 asserts that the involution obtained by exchanging the two preimages in each fiber of the displayed quadrinomial is nonlinear.
